changelog: 3.0.0 — IA v3. The eight flat tabs now sort by ONE axis, the job you came to do, under four group headings: Understand / Decide / Build / Submit. TLDR stays ungrouped above them and Documents stays chrome below them. THE GROUP LABELS NAME INTENTS, NEVER STATES — no active group, no progress, no numbering, and nothing in the pack may drive their appearance, because a lifecycle in a nav is how the old six-step stage stepper became a lie. Rules & Requirements splits back into two tabs, since the split IS the difference: `rules` (Rules of the bid, governs the bid, read-only) and `compliance` (Delivery scope, what we deliver if we win). `compliance` keeps its id because shared links pointed at requirements, and `rules` stops being a SECTION_ALIAS so old #/…/rules links land on the right half. Program dates move from readiness to Delivery scope, so each view carries ONE clock: the kind filter chips and the two-color key are gone as redundant, and the TODAY marker no longer appears on the client's own dates. NEW: Pre-flight, the view for the moment of submitting — deadline, format and delivery, a one-time confirmation pass over the rules (writing `rules[].checked`, the field nothing had read since the rules checklist was removed, because a pass genuinely completes where a rule never does), anything still open, and the attachment list. TLDR gains one strip naming what is waiting on you, shown only when we know who is reading and they own something open. The host now lands you on the section you last visited per pursuit; first-time readers still get TLDR. Renames: Readiness→Our readiness, Scorecard→Scoring & fit, Team & Burden→Effort & team, Questions→Questions to client, and every page title now matches its nav item. Rules of the bid and Delivery scope are now formatted as siblings: both group their rows through listBlock and both put date content in a fold rendered by the same timeline() component. Rules group by `rules[].category` (Eligibility / Format & limits / Required forms / Delivery), inferred from the label when absent, with anything unplaceable in a visible Unclassified group — the rules collection had been attracting strategy notes and evaluation criteria, and a flat list hid them. Design-system pass so no section needs re-learning: risks and signals now go through listBlock like every other list (listBlock gained a second filter axis, `axis:"sev"`, giving risks High/Medium/Low chips with the same CSS-flip behavior as status), the bespoke signal list with colored dashes for bullets is gone — direction is carried by the group name, which is unambiguous — severity moved into the shared row's id column, and the risk detail's two prose blocks are labeled "Proposed mitigation" and "How we answer it in the proposal" instead of sitting unlabeled. ONE disclosure chevron for the whole brief: the expander drew a CSS chevron while folds and collapse headers rendered a solid triangle from a .rb-caret span, and the risk summary carried both at once — that was the double caret, not a native browser marker. .rb-caret survives only on the export menu, which is not a disclosure. Competencies map legacy free-text names onto the ten areas of expertise ON READ (Cyber → DevSecOps & Service Management, QA → Quality & Test Automation, and so on), leading with the canonical area and keeping the pack's original wording underneath as "stated as …", so pursuits imported before the vocabulary closed read correctly without a re-run; a name that cannot be placed with confidence stays unmapped rather than guessed at. EVERYTHING IS EDITABLE: roster, competencies, key personnel, requirements, scoring criteria, success criteria, signals, decisions, parking lot and meetings all gained add/edit/delete. That needed three changes underneath — applyOverrides removes by any field (`itemKey`, or `@index` for arrays of plain strings), setByPath accepts positional selectors and nested collection paths, and add/remove resolve dotted collections like `team.competencies` instead of writing to a literal key nothing reads. Pre-flight stays read-only apart from its rule ticks, because everything on it is derived from other sections.

2.2.0 — naming and modelling pass, all of it correction rather than rename. Plan becomes READINESS and argues from the number down: score, then the linked blockers that explain it (deriveReadiness().gaps now returns {text,goto,el} objects), then the checklist, then the dates last because dates are the frame not the content. Compliance becomes RULES & REQUIREMENTS and the split is stated: 'To bid at all, we must obey this' / 'If we win, we deliver this' — miss a rule and the bid is discarded unread, miss a requirement and you priced work you cannot do. A RULE IS NOT A TASK: the rules checkbox, the 'N of M confirmed' count and the readiness input built on `checked` are gone, so readiness has two honest inputs instead of three with one invented. The must/mandatory/gate chips are gone everywhere; `mandatory` stays in the data because rowStatus() derives atRisk from it. The coverage matrix is gone. Scorecard becomes EVALUATION SCORECARD. FTE is gone from Team & Burden, replaced by two hour estimates per competency — hours (analog) and hoursAi — with a chip toggle and the saving as a percentage, offered only when the pack carries hoursAi. Competencies are a closed vocabulary: the ten Experis areas of expertise in published order, off-menu entries rendered and flagged. Two CSS faults fixed that had silently disabled every filter chip's border: a class selector losing to the `.rb button {border:0}` reset, and the never-defined --rb-rule token.

2.1.0 — three fixes and one behavior change. (1) KEY DATES carry a kind: response dates are ours to hit, program dates are the client's own, and the two are color-coded with a key and filtered one at a time — a rail mixing 'in 4 days' with 'in 14 months' made the far date read as slack on the near one. dates[].kind is honoured where the pack states it and inferred from the label where it does not; the countdown tile's 'Next' now ignores program dates, which is why it was pointing at a milestone a year out. (2) TICK TO CLOSE: action items, requirements and submission rules can be marked done from read mode. Closing a row was behind the edit button, which is a mode you have to know exists; the tick writes the same override and the same activity row. (3) The Plan tab's 'who's carrying what' heatmap is gone — on a real pursuit it was a grid of ones and zeroes above a checklist already grouped by owner. Also: data-goto anchors now carry their real route instead of href='#', one heading over Key dates instead of two, and a document link the site is carrying resolves on click rather than blocking first paint on every attached PDF.

2.0.0 — the V2 information architecture, from four user-feedback sessions. Twelve nav sections become EIGHT: Snapshot absorbs The Ask (Scope); Key Dates + Action Checklist become Plan; Rules & Constraints + Requirements become Compliance; Evaluation + Pass/Fail Gates become Scorecard; Decisions & Parking Lot becomes Record, last. Document Map leaves the nav and sits as a separate launcher at its foot. Every list now shares one component: filter chips driven by its own statuses plus Mine, collapsible groups with persisted state, and a three-state status token (done | open | atRisk) that means the same thing everywhere — filtering is a CSS state flip, never a re-render, so it cannot disturb edit mode or fight live sync. Team & Burden estimates in HOURS not fractional FTE, with effort distribution; 'Current load' renamed because it read as personal availability. Risk detail collapses behind an expander and renders a suggested strategic response. Soft signals replaces 'beige'. The 'must' chip is suppressed when every row carries it. Old section routes (ask, checklist, dates, rules, requirements) resolve through aliases so shared links survive.

1.2.0 — live edit sync: elements, activity and the pursuit index now stream over onSnapshot instead of being read once at load, so another person's edit reaches the open brief without a reload. Remote changes park while a field is focused and land on blur, so a re-render can never eat what someone is typing. Comment listener reconnects with backoff instead of degrading permanently on one blip. schemaSupport raised to 4. editMode declared honestly — it shipped in 1.1.x but the manifest still said false.
1.1.0 — visual craft pass: one type scale, one row grid, one chip system, controlled measure, masthead + countdown pill, inline source disclosure, AA-safe greys.
1.0.0 — first release: 12 sections read mode, four derived components, document previews.
notes: Fetch renderer.js + renderer.css from this directory and inline both to build a standalone brief. Do not fork — improvements here re-render every hosted pursuit on redeploy. Section IDS are preserved across the 12->8 merge and SECTION_ALIASES maps the retired ones, because #/b/<pursuit>/requirements links are already shared in Teams threads; a tidier id set is not worth a dead link. Document bytes are base64-chunked into pursuits/{briefId}/files — deploy firestore.rules alongside a renderer that expects them, or every fetch fails closed.
